reasoning_traces.think:
The paper introduces a novel mechanism for betting on permutations using a convex parimutuel call-auction framework. It distinguishes two betting types: fixed reward (NP-hard) and proportional (polynomial-time solvable). The key innovation lies in transforming the complex permutation outcome space into manageable marginal price structures. Using the Convex Parimutuel Call Auction Model (CPCAM), the organizer maximizes worst-case profit subject to constraints ensuring liquidity and consistency. Marginal prices are recovered uniquely via dual variables, forming a doubly stochastic matrix Q. From these marginals, a max-entropy joint distribution is reconstructed using exponential family parametrization. This process involves solving a convex program whose dual provides the marginal prices, and whose primal yields the probability mass function over permutations. The computational tractability hinges on reformulating the proportional betting LP into a compact form via matching polytope integrality and LP duality. The resulting distribution approximates the true joint via FPTAS for the permanent, offering polynomial-time guarantees under certain conditions. However, this framework fails to address GSE's core needs because GSE does not operate a betting exchange, nor does it rely on external market prices for its predictive models.
